gallery.description:
'George' is one of four similar diesels which run the bulk of the services.
Built in Leeds by Hunslet in 1992, No12 is named after George Thomas, 1st Viscount Tonypandy.
All four diesels are powered by a turbo-charged six-cylinder Rolls-Royce engine giving 319hp.
Llanberis Station.
Snowdon Mountain Railway.
Wales.

26-5-2013

gallery.filename: Path and Line run in Tandem - geograph.org.uk - 244267.jpg
gallery.title: File:Path and Line run in Tandem - geograph.org.uk - 244267.jpg
gallery.description: Path and Line run in Tandem. This photograph shows the Llanberis Path and the Snowdon Mountain Railway track as they climb up the slope in the direction of Half Way House and Half Way Station respectively. In the foreground the railway line runs below the path. In the middle ground the railway crosses the path by means of a bridge and climbs above it to Half Way Station (both hidden in this view). The path continues on towards Half Way House which can be seen clearly.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

gallery.filename: Caterpillar digger on Snowdon Mountain Railway - geograph.org.uk - 1174826.jpg
gallery.title: File:Caterpillar digger on Snowdon Mountain Railway - geograph.org.uk - 1174826.jpg
gallery.description: Caterpillar digger on Snowdon Mountain Railway This digger is the means by which the rail track is dug out of the winter snow.  There is still a significant amount of snow to be moved before it reaches the station.  The shadowy figures of walkers can be seen on the path above the railway.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland
Taken with Canon Digital IXUS 870 IS

gallery.filename: Danger-Perygl on the Snowdon Mountain Railway - geograph.org.uk - 1174932.jpg
gallery.title: File:Danger-Perygl on the Snowdon Mountain Railway - geograph.org.uk - 1174932.jpg
gallery.description: Danger/Perygl on the Snowdon Mountain Railway It is not immediately obvious but the track of the Snowdon Mountain Railway is beneath the snow here.  The 'Danger/Perygl' sign is to warn walkers to stay clear of the track when the trains are running.  They were not running on this day.  The path to the summit can be seen on the right.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland
Taken with Canon Digital IXUS 870 IS

gallery.filename: New station building on Yr Wyddfa - geograph.org.uk - 1174963.jpg
gallery.title: File:New station building on Yr Wyddfa - geograph.org.uk - 1174963.jpg
gallery.description: New station building on Yr Wyddfa The new station building and platform, which has been built to serve the Snowdon Mountain Railway, looks particularly grey on this misty day.  This building doesn't seem to have received as much publicity as the shapely cafe building beyond.  I wonder why?

gallery.filename: One in five to the station on Yr Wyddfa - geograph.org.uk - 1174750.jpg
gallery.title: File:One in five to the station on Yr Wyddfa - geograph.org.uk - 1174750.jpg
gallery.description: One in five to the station on Yr Wyddfa The sign at the side of the Snowdon Mountain railway indicates that the gradient is 1 in 5 from here to the station.  The footpath to the summit is higher up to the left but the gradient isn't any better.
